problem: The company wanted to cut costs and speed up customer service.
title: Klarna leans on AI for customer service, then rehires human agents
context: Klarna said its AI assistant handled about two-thirds of customer chats and did the work of 700 agents, and the company froze hiring.
decision_made: Rely heavily on AI for customer service instead of hiring human agents.
action_taken: In 2025 the CEO said cost had been too dominant a factor and the company began recruiting human agents again, while expanding AI use.
observed_outcome: The CEO said the AI approach led to lower quality; Klarna started recruiting human agents in a new model. Coverage differs on whether this is a full retreat or a hybrid.
lessons: Optimising mainly for cost can lower service quality; a hybrid of AI and people may work better.
limitations: Based on secondary coverage of CEO statements, not the full interview. Results beyond quality remarks were not documented.

claims.claim_text: Klarna had pushed AI to replace human customer service work and froze hiring.
The CEO said the AI push lowered service quality and Klarna began recruiting human agents again.
